neighbours.label: naming the assumed or extreme case behind an estimate or design basis: 'worst case', 'most optimistic assumptions', a rated load or magnitude to withstand
fire: The levee was built for the worst case storm surge on record.
Even with the most pessimistic assumptions, the fund stays solvent.
The tower is designed to survive a 9.0 magnitude quake.
Engineers sized the pumps for a worst case scenario of total power loss.
Under the most favourable assumptions, the mine pays back in six years.
The roof must be capable of carrying a 500 kg snow load.
Planners budgeted for the worst case, in which every unit fails at once.
The shelter is rated to withstand a 250 km/h wind.
quiet: The levee was rebuilt after the storm surge of last autumn.
Even with the new manager, the fund stays in the same office.
The tower was damaged by a quake in the spring of 1994.
Engineers replaced the pumps after a total loss of power in June.
Under the new owners, the mine reopened six years ago.
The roof collapsed under the snow during the night.
Planners met on Tuesday, when every unit was inspected at once.
The shelter was flattened by the wind last winter.

notes: Card: worst case, end of life, middle-of-the-road scenario, most optimistic assumptions, 'withstand a 7.5-magnitude'; the pole's output promotes ' scenario', ' worst', ' hypothetical', ' assuming'. Probes: 0.21-0.63 on such phrases, 0.01-0.03 on the same topics stated as plain events.
